text.p: France's top anti-terrorist judge remanded Corsica's best-known hardline separatist leader and his girlfriend in custody on Wednesday, justice sources said.

Judge Jean-Louis Bruguiere formally placed Francois Santoni and Marie-Helene Mattei under investigation on suspicion of being accomplices to bomb attacks, attempted extortion, belonging to a banned group in connection with terrorist activities and recreating a banned organisation.
Santoni is the leader of Cuncolta Naziunalista, the legal wing of the outlawed Corsican National Liberation Front (FLNC)-Historic Wing.

The FLNC's hardline wing has claimed responsibility for a recent series of bomb attacks on the Mediterranean island and the French mainland, including the bombing of the Bordeaux mayoral office of Prime Minister Alain Juppe.
Santoni surrendered to police on Monday after they detained Mattei in connection with a bomb attack against a Corsican golf course whose owner had refused to pay "revolutionary tax".
Santoni had been on the run for four months after being sentenced to four months in prison for carrying guns.
